newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Turnpike awards $500 mln toll contract to MFS.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Turnpike awards $500 mln toll contract to MFS.

text.p: The New Jersey Turnpike Authority said Tuesday it awarded a $500 million contract to MFS Network Technologies Inc. for an electronic toll collection system.

The contract, which the authority said is the largest of its kind in the nation, came after the state Assembly on Monday passed legislation authorizing the so-called EZ Pass system. The Senate passed the measure earlier this month, and Gov. Christine Whitman is expected to sign it.
Lockheed Martin Corp., however, is contesting the award of the contract to MFS, arguing that the selection process was tainted.

The Turnpike's award came on behalf of a consortium of transportation agencies that will use the system, including the New Jersey Highway Authority, South Jersey Transportation Authority, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, and the Delaware Deparment of Transportation.
"The award of this contract is a significant step toward the goal of full implementation of a regional electronic toll collection system," Joseph Miele, commissioner of the Turnpike Authority, said.

When fully implemented over the next several years, drivers will be able to travel the entire system of roadways without ever having to pay cash for a toll. Instead, an electronic reader will automatically deduct the required toll from the driver's pre-paid account as the car passes through a toll booth.

"Our system will also be compatible and interoperable with EZ Pass on the New York Thruway and the bridges and tunnels operated by the Metropolitan Transportation Authority," Edward Gross, the Turnpike's executive director, said.
Full operation is expected on the Turnpike and Garden State Parkway in eighteen months, and on the Atlantic City Expressway before the end of 1997.
